E2ESeedCacheTests.test_seed_snapshot_is_.obsolete: The SQLite E2E seed cache builds a seeded storage root once per worker and clones its files into each test's root. A PostgreSQL E2E server is seeded with rows in its own disposable database before it starts (AppServer.start calls seed_postgres_library and never _materialize_seed), so there is no file template to cache, clone or reuse.

E2ESeedCacheTests.test_cache_can_be_disa.obsolete: The SQLite E2E seed cache builds a seeded storage root once per worker and clones its files into each test's root. A PostgreSQL E2E server is seeded with rows in its own disposable database before it starts (AppServer.start calls seed_postgres_library and never _materialize_seed), so there is no file template to cache, clone or reuse. PRKS_E2E_SEED_CACHE has nothing to switch off.

E2ESeedCacheTests.test_seeded_pdf_index_.note: On PostgreSQL the seed adopts the managed PDFs and queues their text jobs for the server's worker; a repeated text job for unchanged bytes extracts nothing again.

E2ESeedCacheTests.test_seeded_index_dete.note: A PostgreSQL Asset's bytes change only through a replace, which records the new hash, drops the old text and queues a new extraction; the SQLite file fingerprint check has no counterpart.

E2ESeedCacheTests.test_finalize_checkpoi.obsolete: It covers finalizing the SQLite seed template: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE), the -wal and -shm companions, and refusing a template that an open SQLite writer holds. A PostgreSQL seed is committed rows in the server's own database, with no database file to checkpoint or copy, so the WAL handling goes with the SQLite seed cache.
